title: Console request archetype matrix and intake acceptance checklist
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We receive a heterogeneous stream of console and reporting requests from enterprise customers (usage exports, tenant cost breakdowns, custom dashboards, ad-hoc analytics). Current intake is ad-hoc: requests lack consistent evidence, required artifacts, and observability requirements. This slows TTM, increases back-and-forth, and causes misrouting to the wrong delivery lane.

Goal: Create a single-page intake acceptance checklist + an "archetype matrix" that maps request attributes to triage outcomes (self-serve, priority PM backlog, dedicated projects, professional services) and required artifacts. The artifact set should standardize what engineering/design needs to estimate and deliver within SLA bands.

Scope: Enterprise console/reporting requests that are NOT bugs. Includes usage analytics exports, tenant-level cost breakdowns, scheduled reports, custom dashboard builds, and ad-hoc data slices for legal/compliance review. Excludes infra-only work (ENG-only infra upgrades), billing system changes owned by Finance, and incident remediation.

Deliverables: 1) Intake acceptance checklist (fields + mandatory evidence). 2) Archetype matrix (rows = request archetypes; columns = required artifacts, priority lane, estimated lead time, typical owner, activation criteria). 3) Routing rules for the Console triage board and a sample intake form template (Confluence + web form). 4) Example mappings for 6 recent enterprise asks and recommended lane outcomes. 5) Hand-off playbook for PM -> ENG/Design -> Customer Success (CS).

Success metrics: reduce clarification cycles by 50% on new requests; reduce time-to-first-estimate from 6 business days to 2 business days; increase percent of requests correctly routed on first pass to 85%.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes on evidence: For cost breakdown and export asks we require: workspace ID(s), tenant sample size, target time window, expected cardinality, example CSV of desired output, SLAs (latency, recurrence), and customer contact/owner. For dashboards: target users, AZ/regional constraints, column-level access rules, and whether PII is present.

Suggested intake fields (minimum): requester name, workspace, workspace tier, business justification, archetype selection (checkboxes), ask priority (customer SLO vs business priority), evidence attachments, desired delivery window, compliance flags, acceptance test definition, contact for follow-up.

Routing heuristics (examples): - If "requires new schema or ETL" + high cardinality -> flow to Dedicated Projects lane (long lead). - If "CSV export of existing telemetry" + low cardinality + scheduled recurrence -> Self-serve/Scheduled Reports lane. - If customer requests SLA-backed delivery with audit trail -> Enterprise Professional Services lane (commercial scope).
acceptance_criteria: Intake checklist published in Confluence with example filled form
Archetype matrix covers at least 6 distinct request archetypes and includes recommended lane and artifact sets
Routing rules configured as 3 automations on the Console triage board (self-serve, PM backlog, professional services)
Sample intake form template created and a pilot with 2 enterprise accounts completed
SLOs for time-to-first-estimate and routing accuracy defined and instrumented in triage board metrics
